body.summary: Every flip is derived from HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the server seed, over the message clientSeed:nonce:block. Flip i reads draw i: four bytes at offset 4i of the stream, as a big-endian unsigned 32-bit integer u; the block is the byte cursor divided by 32, so flips 1..8 come from block 0 and flips 9..10 from block 1. The side is side = floor(u / 2^32 * 2): 0 = H, 1 = T. A round of n calls and a target wins iff at least target of the n calls land as called (target = n unless chosen: every flip); in the target game a win pays floor4(0.99 * 2^n / S(n, target)), S(n, k) = sum_{i>=k} C(n, i); = 0.99 * 2^n when target = n (a 1% edge: the return is at most 99% at every n and target, exactly 99% where the multiplier is a short number) and a loss pays 0. The smallest target at each n keeps the win chance at or under 98%. In Multi Toss the same flips settle a different bet: multi toss: the stake is split over the n coins; every coin that lands as called pays its share at 1.98x, so h of n coins pay floor4(1.98 * h / n), h = coins landed as called (2 <= n <= 10) (each coin is an even-money bet at 99%, so the round returns at most 99%). With coins set, coins x flips: C coins (2..10) each flip the F-letter calls pattern in a row; coin i reads draws i*F .. i*F+F-1; every coin whose F flips all land as called pays its share at 0.99 * 2^F, so the round pays floor4(0.99 * 2^F * h / C), h = coins that survived all F flips (each coin is a streak bet at exactly 99%, so the round returns at most 99%). This is the standard Coin Flip formula: any public verifier that reads the HMAC stream and takes the top bit of each draw prints the same flips. The server seed is committed up front by its SHA-256 hash and revealed when you rotate, so a result can never be changed after the fact.
